title: Crase (à) in Depth
summary: Understand when preposition a combines with feminine articles and pronouns to form à.

sections.heading: What crase is
sections.body: **Crase** is the written accent marking the contraction of the preposition **a** with a feminine article or pronoun: **a + a = à**, **a + as = às**. It is not a pronunciation stress mark.

examples.en: I am going to the pharmacy.
I handed the report to the teacher.

sections.heading: When there is no crase
sections.body: There is no crase before masculine words, most verbs, indefinite articles, or plural feminine nouns without the plural article **as**.

sections.heading: Useful tests and fixed expressions
sections.body: If you can replace the feminine noun with a masculine one and get **ao**, crase is likely: vou à escola → vou ao banco. Many adverbial expressions with feminine nouns take crase.

examples.note: repeated words usually do not take crase

keyPoints: Crase marks a + a/as, written à/às.
It depends on both the preceding word requiring a and the following feminine article/pronoun.
No crase before verbs or masculine nouns.
The ao substitution test is useful but not perfect.

commonMistakes.note: No article before pé in this expression.
Entregar a + a professora = à professora.
